newsitem.title: UK: Clinton praises monetary independence for BOE.
newsitem.headline: Clinton praises monetary independence for BOE.

text.p: President Bill Clinton praised Britain's new Labour government on Thursday for its decision to give the Bank of England freedom to set interest rates.
Speaking at a Downing Street news conference with Prime Minister Tony Blair, Clinton said:

"I think the prime minister did a good thing -- and he'll be criticised for it the first time interest rates are raised -- by trying to take the setting of interest rates out of politics, because it will create the feeling of stability and make Britain more attractive for investment."

Within days of its landslide election victory on May 1, the new government ceded control over interest rates -- previously the prerogative of the Chancellor of the Exchequer -- to a new monetary policy committee at the Bank of England.
The committee holds its first meeting on June 6.
